newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA LOSES 4.4 MLN RAND ON FOOD-FOR-KIDS PLAN.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA LOSES 4.4 MLN RAND ON FOOD-FOR-KIDS PLAN.

text.p: South Africa's ambitious plan to feed poverty-stricken primary school kids had lost 4.38 million rand to fraud or misspending, opposition party leader Tony Leon said on Tuesday.
Leon, leader of the Democratic Party, said in a statement the figure was contained in a reply from Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma to questions he put in parliament.
"The reply reveals a shocking and depressing picture of mismanagement and misappropriation of funds," Leon said.
"The total amount of 4.38 million rand known to have been stolen, defrauded or misappropriated means... the opportunity to provide 7.98 million meals to hungry children has been lost," he said.
The scheme was introduced by President Nelson Mandela's government shortly after it took office in May 1994 and was one of its first tangible bids to improve the lives of impoverished blacks.
